summary.intent: Run the GSD manager command center to discuss, plan, and execute three gap-closure phases (42: API unpin integrity, 43: FUSE write durability, 44: IPNS conflict handling) surfaced by a UAT audit on the CipherBox repo.
summary.outcome: Phase 42 was fully completed and closed (8 plans, 3 waves, all gates green, todos archived). Phase 43 was executed through 8 plans across 6 waves including a gap-closure loop; the transcript ends at wave-6 merged with tracking committed but before the final re-review/re-verify/phase.complete pipeline. Phase 44 was discussed and had a CONTEXT.md written but was not yet planned or executed.

repo: The unpin endpoint POST /ipfs/unpin is publicly accessible to any account holder — JwtAuthGuard only, no ownership check, open signup via Web3Auth. The handler never reads req.user, passing any CID straight to Kubo.

Kubo runs with the 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72). The server profile only disables local-network discovery; full public DHT participation means every pinned CID's provider records are publicly harvestable.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without calling unpin (shared-write.ts:450), so there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path — any cross-user call is malicious or erroneous.
eslint already ignores .planning/ and .claude/ but .prettierignore did not exist, causing prettier to mangle planning markdown and break a testPathPattern pipe in VALIDATION.md into a table column.

pnpm --filter @pkg test -- --testPathPattern=X is broken: pnpm inserts a bare '--' separator that makes jest treat the flag as a positional regex. Correct form: pnpm --filter @pkg exec jest --testPathPattern='X'.

1Password SSH commit signing requires dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true on Bash tool calls; agent signing errors require restarting the 1Password desktop app. Never use --no-gpg-sign as PRs enforce signatures.
gsd commit helper returns 'committed: false' as a false negative on success. Always verify with git log before retrying.

BYO unpin is broken in both directions today; the new guardedUnpin fixes server-side semantics ('not pinned' is now silently swallowed) without requiring BYO provider.unpin client wiring changes in this phase.
The upload-compensation path (ipfs.controller.ts:122) fires a global pin/rm which can destroy another user's content-addressed deduped blob — rerouted through guardedUnpin as part of phase 42.

Cross-compilation of WinFsp crates on macOS fails for pre-existing unrelated reasons (windows-future, winfsp-sys registry crates); use cargo check instead of cargo build --features winfsp on macOS CI.

code.finding: Kubo configured with 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (tcp+udp). Server profile only disables local-network discovery, not DHT participation — all pinned CIDs are publicly advertised.
Writable-share save drops prunedCids array without issuing any unpin call, so there is no legitimate cross-user unpin scenario in the codebase.
Upload-compensation path fires a global pin/rm that can destroy another user's content-addressed blob. Rerouted through VaultService.guardedUnpin in phase 42.

guardedUnpin added: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid)) → transactional row-delete + refcount → pending_unpins outbox insert if last reference → Kubo pin/rm post-commit best-effort. Silent 2XX for no-row calls with cross-user audit metric.
New entity @Entity('pending_unpins') with unique cid index and no userId — stores outbox entries for Kubo pin/rm operations to survive crashes.
Full rewrite: JournalOp enum, JournalEntry with status lifecycle, WriteQueue with put/remove/load_all_for_vault/update_status/record_failure/ordered_for_replay. Persistence-backed with fsync barrier.

CR-04: EIO reply added on journal fsync failure so OS is not acked after error. CR-08: spawn_journal.remove moved out of background upload thread; replay-on-mount is the authoritative cleanup path. CR-07: journal_entry_snapshot carried into spawn for record_failure on max retries.

journal-fsync-before-ack ordering enforced: journal.put → handle.cleanup → reply.ok → spawn → journal.remove-on-success. MkdirPublish journaled before reply.entry; conflict arm sends FsEvent::MkdirConflict instead of warn-only.
New security alert provisioned in 'CipherBox Security' rule group: rate(cipherbox_unpin_cross_user_attempts_total[5m]) > 0 threshold.

WorkerHost with drainPendingUnpins (calls provider not raw Kubo, error-isolates per row, publishes gauge) and runDriftReport (NDJSON parse, read-only — zero .delete() in drift path to prevent accidental GC).

workflow: GSD worktree cleanup-wave is not idempotent: already-merged entries report branch_mismatch on rerun. Write reduced manifests containing only remaining unmerged entries for reruns.
cleanup-wave must run from the repo root, not from inside an agent worktree — it resolves repoRoot from cwd, causing false base_mismatch errors when called from a worktree path.
Node_modules and .husky/_ untracked dirs in agent worktrees block merge cleanup. Rm them before running cleanup-wave. Later executor prompts should include an explicit CLEANUP instruction.
A merge that resolves all conflicts but fails the commit step leaves MERGE_HEAD. Use git commit --no-edit to conclude, then manually rm the worktree and delete its branch.
nest build reformats openapi.json as a side effect (hundreds of formatting-only lines). Run git checkout -- openapi.json before merging Wave N+1 worktrees to avoid false conflict noise.
For the decision-coverage mechanical grep gate, PLAN.md must_haves need literal 'D-NN:' citation strings — the grep is exact-string, not semantic.
When a planner agent dies mid-run (socket error), verify which plan files are complete on disk before spawning a continuation planner to avoid duplicate or overwritten plans.
Per-CID advisory xact lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid))) closes the concurrent-unpin race that would strand orphaned pins even with a transactional outbox.
The read-only drift report (pin ls diff vs pinned_cids ∪ pending_unpins) should detect and log only — never auto-delete — to avoid GC footgun on pins the relay path didn't create.

Spawning executors in isolated git worktrees prevents merge conflicts across parallel plan execution but requires careful base-SHA tracking per wave; capture the SHA immediately before dispatching each wave.

friction: 1Password SSH signing failed mid-session with 'agent returned an error / fatal: failed to write commit object' — required user to restart the 1Password desktop app before commits could land.
gsd commit helper reported 'committed: false' as a false negative multiple times while commits had actually landed, causing unnecessary retry confusion and wasted tool calls.
cleanup-wave run from wrong cwd (inside a worktree) produced false base_mismatch failures for all entries, requiring a full rerun from repo root.
cleanup-wave is not idempotent — running it twice on the same manifest blocked on already-merged entries with branch_mismatch, requiring manual manifest reduction to remaining-only entries.
Worktree cruft (node_modules dirs, .husky/_ shim) blocked git operations during merge cleanup across multiple waves.
42-05 merge left MERGE_HEAD after conflicts were auto-resolved but the commit step failed, requiring manual git commit --no-edit and then manual worktree rm + branch -D.
openapi.json formatting drift (nest build side effect) injected hundreds of spurious diff lines before Wave 3 merges, requiring git checkout -- to restore.
Planner agent disconnected with socket error after writing plans 01-03, requiring filesystem verification and a continuation planner for plans 04-08.
pnpm/jest flag-forwarding bug (pnpm inserts bare '--' separator) caused jest to misparse --testPathPattern as a positional regex, requiring a workaround on every targeted test run.
Session quota limits interrupted execution mid-wave twice, causing task-notification duplication confusion on resume and requiring re-dispatch of already-running executors.
User sent accidental free-text input ('touring wyatt web bossy') twice mid-execution, triggering tool rejections and flow interruptions.
D-07 decision coverage gate failed on first pass because the mechanical grep requires a literal 'D-07:' string and the plan lacked the exact citation token.
prettier mangled VALIDATION.md table (broke a regex pipe into a table column) because .prettierignore did not exist — discovered mid-planning, not at write time.
